correctness.rationale: The centered fundamental-domain law is a product of independent uniform coordinates. The entire MGF factorization is exact; F has a nonzero zero by the zero-free Hadamard theorem for order <=1 and positive variance, and each zero is simple by \(F(z)+2zF\prime(z)=\exp(z)\). The closest-zero peeling thus returns each maximal period and its multiplicity before division. Exact cumulant formulas and Newton identities give the d=3 inverse, and rationally distinct triples certify the first-two-moment insufficiency. The package runs exact and numerical independent checks, without treating finite numerical root searches as proof of least modulus.

originality.rationale: The accessible full arXiv texts of Boutin–Kemper (2003) and Mémoli–Needham (2018/2022), plus the available Osada source, and six actual semantic published-finding corpus queries were compared at object, distance metric, inverse implication, and parameter level. The nearest prior flat-torus counterexample is nonrectangular and dimension two; the nearest positive distance-result concerns finite point sets. No observed result implies the exact rectangular d>=3 zero-peeling rigidity and sharp d=3 moment prefix. This is best-knowledge, not an exhaustive priority certificate.
residual_risks: Some further research literature may independently treat the same rectangular-torus inverse problem; index search cannot establish historical priority.

value.rationale: Distances between uniform points are natural intrinsic metric-measure invariants, known to fail injectivity on unrestricted flat tori. A positive all-dimensional rigidity theorem for the structurally motivated orthogonal subclass and an exactly optimal three-scalar recovery in d=3 resolve a meaningful quantitative inverse problem. The analytic zero peeling and tight 2-vs-3 moment boundary are structural, not arbitrary moment tabulation.
